entries.title: Lección Primera
journal: First day. The reading and comprehension were easy, although I suspect that is because I have used some of the language apps out there and already know a little Spanish. I also listened to a couple of YouTube videos, just to get the accent into my ear.
I am worried that I sound very English, but my Spanish friend assures me that she does not care as long as she understands me.

The lesson was quick, and I definitely feel that the old-style method of reading, writing in a notebook, hearing myself, underlining and speaking made me learn in a way I have not for a long time. When I do these things digitally, I often feel that I am doing them passively. This time I felt much more involved.

entries.title: Lección Segunda
entries.todaySpanish: Poco a poco — little by little.
journal: I came to Lección II and the reading and comprehension were fine — until I started circling words. It took me a long time to work out the differences between children, girls and boys. That is simply the way my brain works.
I looked up words using an old-fashioned dictionary rather than an online translator. That gave me time to digest the words and think about them properly.

The lesson was longer, so I split it over two days: first reading and writing out the conversation, then a quick recap the next day before answering the questions. I was mostly confident, although I was uncertain about one or two answers.
In the modern world we have AI, so I asked it to read Lección II and compare my answers. I photographed the pages in my notebook and was reassured by the feedback.
I am definitely beginning to feel more confident. Roll on the next lesson!
